verifications.claim: The IRS failure-to-file penalty is typically 5% of the unpaid taxes for each month or part of a month a tax return is late.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The late filing penalty is 5% of the additional taxes owed amount for every month (or fraction thereof) your return is late" (R1); "The failure-to-file penalty is usually five percent of the tax owed for each month, or part of a month" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the 5% per month or part of month for failure-to-file on unpaid taxes.

verifications.claim: The IRS failure-to-file penalty is capped at 25% of the unpaid tax.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "up to a maximum of 25%" (R1); "up to a maximum of 25%" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant references explicitly confirm the 25% cap on failure-to-file penalty.

verifications.claim: The failure-to-pay penalty is 0.5% per month.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The late payment penalty is 0.5% of the additional tax owed amount for every month (or fraction thereof)" (R1); "The failure-to-pay penalty is one-half of one percent for each month" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as 0.5% per month across references.

verifications.claim: If you also fail to pay on time, the failure-to-file penalty is reduced by the failure-to-pay penalty.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the late filing penalty will be reduced by the amount of the late payment penalty applied in that month. For example, instead of a 5% late filing penalty for the month, the IRS would apply a 4.5% late filing penalty and a 0.5% late payment penalty" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported with examples of reduction (e.g., 5% to 4.5%) in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The total penalty for failure-to-file and failure-to-pay combined is 5% per month.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the combined penalty is 5% (4.5% late filing and 0.5% late payment)" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm combined rate remains 5% per month when both apply.

verifications.claim: For returns filed more than 60 days late in 2026, the minimum penalty is the lesser of $525 or 100% of the tax owed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If you file more than 60 days after the due date, the minimum penalty is $525 (for tax returns required to be filed in 2026) or 100% of your unpaid tax, whichever is less" (R1); "lesser of $525 (for tax returns required to be filed in 2026)" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for 2026 returns, $525 or 100%, lesser amount in specified references.

verifications.claim: If you are owed a refund, there is no penalty for filing late.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "No penalty if you're getting a tax refund" (R1); "If you’re owed a refund, there’s no fee for filing late" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state no penalty if due a refund.

verifications.claim: The IRS charges interest on unpaid taxes, currently around 7% annually, adjusted quarterly.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The current annual interest rate is 7%" (R8); "The interest rate set by the IRS changes quarterly" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: R8 confirms 7% annual rate; others confirm quarterly adjustment on unpaid taxes.

verifications.claim: Penalties may be waived if you can show "reasonable cause" for the delay (e.g., natural disaster, serious illness).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the IRS may abate your penalties for filing and paying late if you can show reasonable cause" (R2); "possible exceptions for death or serious illness... natural disasters" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for reasonable cause waiver with matching examples.

verifications.claim: The deadline to file a return or extension is April 15.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "don't file your return or extension by April 15, 2026" (R1); "Generally, April 15 is the deadline" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently stated as April 15 for filing returns or requesting extensions.
